instruction:
Load /home/user/Desktop/four_parts.step in FreeCAD 0.21.2 Path/CAM. Run FreeCAD from the terminal with /usr/bin/freecad or /usr/bin/freecadcmd if needed. Use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for FreeCAD Path command-line automation when working on `four_parts.step`.

The STEP must contain four separate identical 60 x 20 x 18 mm rectangular solids with world-coordinate centers G54=(-60,-40), G55=(60,-40), G56=(-60,40), and G57=(60,40) mm and Z=0 at every part bottom. Create four independent native Path Jobs, one per corresponding source solid, in G54, G55, G56, G57 order. Each Job must use its part center/bottom as local (0,0,0), have exactly one matching fixture, preserve an editable source-to-local mapping (SourcePart, SourceSolidIndex, Fixture, WorldCenter, and WorldToLocalTranslation), and use local stock X[-31,31], Y[-11,11], Z[0,19] mm. In every Job, use the same T1 definition: a 10 mm end mill, spindle Forward at S7000 rpm, and horizontal and vertical cutting feeds F500 mm/min. Apply exactly two native operations in this order: (1) MillFace from stock top Z19 to finished top Z18 with 1 mm StepDown, fully covering the 62 x 22 mm stock top; (2) an Outside, CW, geometrically tool-radius-compensated Profile from Z18 to Z0 with 3 mm StepDown and zero extra offset, without cutting into the 60 x 20 mm finished part. Use SafeHeight Z21 and ClearanceHeight Z23 for both operations. Each Job must use the linuxcnc postprocessor, no split output, and /home/user/Desktop/task-09.nc as its configured output. Keep the four Jobs and all eight editable native operations in /home/user/Desktop/task-09.FCStd. Build each Job's real post list, combine the four lists in G54 through G57 order, and run the FreeCAD 0.21.2 LinuxCNC postprocessor once so the single /home/user/Desktop/task-09.nc contains one reachable program with actual Face and Profile cutting under every WCS and only one final program terminator.
